title: On Celebrating the end of the harvest
subtitle: 节日庆典 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 节日庆典（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·节日与庆典）
meta: 主题语境：节日庆典（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·节日与庆典）　|　核心词汇：celebrate　|　正文 352 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 celebrate 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1987 the father ① celebrated the end of the harvest on the same day, and every neighbour in the house said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three months on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the father ② celebrates the end of the harvest before dawn without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ celebrate the end of the harvest at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ celebrated the end of the harvest before — a line in the letter for September 1981 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Celebrating the end of the harvest on the same day, the father said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the chair at the far door, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ celebrate the quiet courage of the old before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Celebrate the quiet courage of the old at once and never mention it again.

By 1994 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the letter, and a new neighbour from the next house ⑧ celebrates the quiet courage of the old on the same day every month without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the door, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ celebrated the end of the harvest again when nobody else would.

⑩ To celebrate the end of the harvest, my mother said in 1999, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the house remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the house forgets, somebody celebrates the end of the harvest before dawn again and somebody must celebrate the end of the harvest on the same day all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 庆祝（一般过去式 celebrated the end of the harvest：1987 年父亲头一回这样做，当天就）
B. v. 庆祝（一般现在 celebrates the end of the harvest：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 庆祝（不定式 to celebrate the end of the harvest：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 庆祝（过去完成时 had celebrated the end of the harvest：1981 年九月的家书上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 庆祝（动名词 celebrating the end of the harvest 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 赞美（celebrate the quiet courage of the old：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去赞美老一辈那份不动声色的勇气）
G. v. 赞美（celebrate the quiet courage of the old：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 庆祝（后段两处：新来的邻居照例 celebrates the quiet courage of the old，而母亲又一次 celebrated the end of the harvest）

answers.why: celebrate 意为“庆祝”，1987 年父亲当天就庆祝庆贺收冬，那是老屋里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 celebrated。
celebrate 意为“庆祝”，自那以后父亲天没亮就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 celebrates。
celebrate 意为“庆祝”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯庆祝庆贺收冬”，此处为不定式 to celebrate the end of the harvest。
celebrate 意为“庆祝”，家书里 九月 那行字说明早在 1994 年之前就有人庆祝过，故用过去完成时 had celebrated。
celebrate 意为“庆祝”，父亲说“庆祝庆贺收冬这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 celebrating the end of the harvest 作主语。
celebrate 意为“赞美”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去赞美老一辈那份不动声色的勇气”，should ever 之后用原形 celebrate the quiet courage of the old。
celebrate 意为“赞美”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻赞美老一辈那份不动声色的勇气（celebrate the quiet courage of the old at once），以后再也不要提起。
celebrate 意为“庆祝”，新来的邻居每个月份都照例赞美老一辈那份不动声色的勇气，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 celebrates。
celebrate 意为“庆祝”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当天就庆祝庆贺收冬，用一般过去式 celebrated 叙述。
celebrate 意为“庆祝”，结尾那句是母亲 1999 年的话：要庆祝庆贺收冬，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和老屋记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 celebrate 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1987 the father celebrated the end of the harvest on the same day, and nobody in the house forgot it.
Even now the father celebrates the end of the harvest before dawn whenever the house asks.
Celebrating the end of the harvest on the same day, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever celebrate the quiet courage of the old before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new neighbour from the next house celebrates the quiet courage of the old on the same day every month, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother celebrated the end of the harvest again, and the house remembered that half.
